0.headline: Biden and His Economic Team Urge Quick Action on Stimulus as Risks Mount
0.abstract: The president-elect introduced key nominees in Delaware, while lawmakers exchanged new proposals with prospects for a deal still dim.

0.headline: The Winds Have Shifted in Pandemic Aid Negotiations
0.abstract: Speaker Nancy Pelosi and Senator Mitch McConnell, the majority leader, spoke on Thursday as Joe Biden’s victory and vaccine breakthroughs added momentum to a push for a stimulus deal.

0.headline: ‘It Makes Me Angry’: These Are the Jobless in a City Filled With Wealth
0.abstract: Pandemic job losses have disproportionately hurt low-paid service workers who tend to be poor and people of color. In this New York neighborhood, hope is slipping away.

0.headline: Use It or Lose It: Tenant Aid Effort Nears a Federal Cutoff
0.abstract: Emergency pandemic funding to help renters must be distributed by Dec. 30. But getting the money to those who need it is no small task.

0.headline: Staring Down Deadline, Congress Nears $900 Billion Stimulus Deal
0.abstract: The emerging compromise would provide emergency stimulus payments, jobless aid and rental assistance, extending help to businesses and funding the distribution of a vaccine. But more is likely to be needed.

0.headline: Congress Strikes Long-Sought Stimulus Deal to Provide $900 Billion in Aid
0.abstract: Democrats and Republicans said they had an agreement on another round of pandemic aid, including direct payments to Americans, jobless benefits and funds for businesses and vaccine distribution.

0.headline: Stimulus Deal Provides Economic Relief, for Now
0.abstract: The aid package will keep millions from losing jobless benefits. But it comes too late to prevent lasting damage to many families and businesses.

0.headline: They’re Young, Unemployed and Facing Bleak Prospects
0.abstract: They worked low-paid jobs in restaurants, stores and theaters. Now they are filing for unemployment at higher rates than before the pandemic.

0.headline: New Signs of Economic Distress Emerge as Trump Imperils Aid Deal
0.abstract: A decline in consumer income and spending poses a further challenge to the recovery as jobless claims remain high and benefits approach a cutoff.

0.headline: A ‘Great Cultural Depression’ Looms for Legions of Unemployed Performers
0.abstract: With theaters and concert halls shuttered, unemployment in the arts has cut deeper than in restaurants and other hard-hit industries.

0.headline: Trump Signs Pandemic Relief Bill After Unemployment Aid Lapses
0.abstract: After calling the measure a “disgrace,” President Trump unexpectedly signed the bill, extending expanded unemployment benefits and an eviction moratorium, and keeping the government open.

0.headline: New York Bans Most Evictions as Tenants Struggle to Pay Rent
0.abstract: The Legislature, addressing hardship caused by the pandemic, convened an unusual special session between Christmas and New Year’s to pass the measure.

0.headline: Trump’s Veto Threat Did Little to Alter Stimulus Package
0.abstract: The president’s threat to scuttle a $900 billion relief package held workers in limbo, but did little to change the bill’s outcome.

0.headline: ‘No Realistic Path’ for Quick Vote on $2,000 Stimulus Checks, McConnell Says
0.abstract: The Senate leader all but ended any chance of increasing direct payments, despite some Republican support for the effort.

0.headline: What Giant Skeletons and Puppy Shortages Told Us About the 2020 Economy
0.abstract: This year was awful, but it gave rise to some interesting social trends. Here’s what they tell us about the economic future.

1.headline: Warning of Shortages, Researchers Look to Stretch Vaccine Supply
1.abstract: The N.I.H. and Moderna are examining whether doses of Moderna’s coronavirus vaccine can be halved to double the supply, while scientists look for other ways to extend availability.

1.headline: With Democrats in Control, Biden Moves to Advance Agenda
1.abstract: By gaining the Senate, Democrats have the chance to move on large parts of the president-elect’s ambitions for the economy, health care, climate change and more.

1.headline: Facing Intensifying Crises, Biden Pledges Action to Address Economy and Pandemic
1.abstract: With job losses, record coronavirus numbers and politics in turmoil after the storming of the Capitol, the president-elect pressed for quick passage of a stimulus package to help struggling Americans.

1.headline: Biden Outlines $1.9 Trillion Spending Package to Combat Virus and Downturn
1.abstract: The president-elect detailed plans for an initial effort to fight the coronavirus and a subsequent one to address economic recovery.

1.headline: Unemployment Claims Rise Sharply, Showing New Economic Pain
1.abstract: Weekly filings for jobless benefits hit the highest level since July as the pandemic’s resurgence batters the service industry.

1.headline: A Second Economic Crisis for Biden, but a Different First Response
1.abstract: The president-elect’s proposed economic rescue package is larger and more targeted to the country’s needs than the stimulus plan he helped steer into law as vice president in 2009.

1.headline: Biden Pledges Federal Vaccine Campaign to Beat a Surging Coronavirus
1.abstract: Facing looming shortages and rising infections, the president-elect promised mobile vaccination sites, National Guard troops and a federal push to increase vaccine production.

1.headline: Biden Seeks Quick Start With Executive Actions and Aggressive Legislation
1.abstract: In an effort to mark a clean break from the Trump era, the president-elect plans to roll out dozens of executive orders in his first 10 days on top of a big stimulus plan and an expansive immigration bill.

1.headline: How Full Employment Became Washington’s Creed
1.abstract: Policymakers are eager to return to the period of low unemployment that preceded the pandemic and are less concerned than in previous eras about sparking inflation and taking on debt.

1.headline: Biden Signs Orders to Expand Food Stamps and Raise Wages, but Says Economy Needs More Help
1.abstract: The president called it an “economic imperative” to provide more aid for millions of Americans who are struggling to make ends meet as the virus exacts a bruising toll.

1.headline: Biden Moves to Expand Health Coverage in Pandemic Economy
1.abstract: President Biden ordered the reopening of Affordable Care Act exchanges and moved to restore coverage mandates and Medicaid plans undermined by his predecessor.

1.headline: Biden Wants the Biggest Stimulus in Modern History. Is It Too Big?
1.abstract: Supporters of a ‘hot’ economy see a chance to correct the mistakes of the last recession. Others see danger.

1.headline: Wall Street Makes Unprecedented Push to Get Out the Vote
1.abstract: Business leaders want their employees to have a say in helping decide who will steer New York City’s economic recovery as its new mayor.

1.headline: Ten G.O.P. senators sketch out their own proposed relief bill in a letter to Biden.
1.abstract: Republican moderates said they could go along with many of the president's proposals if some, like unemployment aid and direct payments, were scaled back.

1.headline: Russia’s Economic Slump Erodes Consensus That Shielded Putin
1.abstract: The rally-around-the-flag effect of President Vladimir V. Putin’s assertive foreign policy known as the Crimea consensus is unraveling with the economy.

2.headline: Republicans Pitch Biden on Smaller Aid Plan as Democrats Prepare to Act Alone
2.abstract: The president met at the White House with Republican senators seeking a much smaller stimulus plan, but congressional Democrats pressed forward to force through his $1.9 trillion measure, if necessary.

2.headline: Anemic Jobs Report Reaffirms Pandemic’s Grip on Economy
2.abstract: With a gain of 49,000 jobs in January, and with few of those in the private sector, the labor market offers little relief to the nearly 10 million Americans who are unemployed.

2.headline: With Economy in ‘Crisis,’ Biden Is Ready to Bypass G.O.P. on Stimulus
2.abstract: President Biden said the economy was in trouble and warned Republicans that he would move ahead with a $1.9 trillion aid package with or without their support.

2.headline: Pandemic’s Toll on Housing: Falling Behind, Doubling Up
2.abstract: Eviction moratoriums don’t keep arrears from piling up, and aid to renters may not reach the most vulnerable.

2.headline: ‘We Are Forgotten’: Grocery Workers Hope for Higher Pay and Vaccinations
2.abstract: Booming business during the pandemic hasn’t always meant better wages, and they have largely been left off vaccine priority lists.

2.headline: ‘The Death Market’: Oxygen Shortage Leaves Mexicans to Die at Home
2.abstract: With hospitals overrun, Mexicans fighting the coronavirus at home face a deadly hurdle: a lack of oxygen tanks.

2.headline: How a Minimum-Wage Increase Is Being Felt in a Low-Wage City
2.abstract: Is $15 an hour too much, or not enough? Fresno, Calif., may be a laboratory for a debate over the minimum wage that is heating up on the national level.

2.headline: Biden Takes Center Stage With Ambitious Agenda as Trump’s Trial Ends
2.abstract: The president plans to quickly press for his $1.9 trillion stimulus bill, and then move on to infrastructure, immigration, climate change and other major priorities.

2.headline: Biden and the Fed Leave 1970s Inflation Fears Behind

11.headline: North Carolina’s Furniture Hub Is Booming. What Comes Next?
11.abstract: The furniture capital of the state is ground zero for inflation, labor shortages, hot demand and limited supply. It’s debating how to cope.

11.headline: Taliban and 9/11 Families Fight for Billions in Frozen Afghan Funds
11.abstract: The White House must figure out what to do with the Afghan central bank’s account at the Federal Reserve, now blocked under U.S. law.
